evidence: NESTING (arithmetic, Pass on the bytes). task/tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template test.sh (diff empty): run_suite gates 1500 (test.sh:213), run_suite scored 11100 (test.sh:224), both under `timeout $budget_sec rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (test.sh:207). task.toml [agent]..[verifier.environment] tail is identical to the template: agent timeout_sec=7200.0, build_timeout_sec=600.0, verifier timeout_sec=13200.0. Gates: render batched timeout=600 (1 criterion), constraints batched timeout=600 (1 criterion); sequential under the shared agent semaphore (rewardkit runner.py:319-321) => 1200 < 1500 (300 s margin). Scored: functional mode='individual' timeout=600 with 15 criteria, polish batched 900 (5), visual batched 900 (5) => 15x600+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s margin). In rewardkit 0.1.7 (pinned harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 in tests/Dockerfile:31) individual agent mode runs each criterion as its own sequential subprocess with asyncio.wait_for(timeout=judge.timeout) (judges.py:467-549), and a timeout zeros only that criterion (probe individual_timeout_retains_first: functional 0.25 with first criterion kept). Gates+scored = 12600 < 13200; liveness probe worst case 120x(2 URLs x 2 s + 0.25 s) ~ 510 s only on a hung app, after which test.sh exits before any suite (test.sh:115-125), so 13200 still bounds the whole run; restart helper waits <= 5 s kill + 30 s ready inside restart_mcp's 55 s, inside one 600 s session. Agent 7200 s and build 600 s equal the frozen template/contract values; the agent Dockerfile is apt (4 packages) + 2 pinned npm globals, a short cold build. The functional judge.toml comment (line 24) records the individual-mode change as the lead's instruction relayed by the owner on 8 Oct 2026 and states the arithmetic correctly; total functional budget (15x600=9000) equals the template's batched functional 9000, so no budget was increased. LONG ENOUGH (unmeasured, credible risk). The template gave functional one shared 9000 s batched session; the candidate gives each of 15 criteria a hard 600 s, i.e. the same per-session value as a one-criterion gate, with no ability to borrow from lighter criteria and only 20 s/criterion of suite headroom (300/15). Each session must also first redo the in-dimension backend check (functional prompt.md:15: sign in, add a candidate, reload, open an independent context via browser_run_code_unsafe, sign in as Observer, find the card) before its own legs. Heavy criteria: hro_manager_roles (2431 chars, 5 replays, 2 independent contexts), hro_unread_seen (2512 chars, negative legs that must watch a full 15 000 ms each plus fresh-context confirmations per prompt.md:29), hro_intake_restart (2382 chars, restart + 3 contexts), hro_bulk / hro_undo (9 and 8 numbered steps, 5 replays each), hro_readonly_roles (Observer + candidate + anonymous replays of ~10 request kinds), hro_candidate (3 replays). Timed observations allow up to 3 attempts (prompt.md:29, Colderwater lesson 7), and lesson 9 requires per-step reporting, both of which add judge turns. With claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx driving Playwright MCP one tool call per LLM round trip, these criteria plausibly need 60-120 tool calls; whether that fits 600 s is not measured. raw-evidence-index.json scope says verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and every entry is 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'; the judge.toml comment itself says 'Not yet measured against a configured judge run.' Per REVIEW_POLICY ('Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number') and SKILL ('Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass'), the 'long enough' half of the row cannot be cleared. Template-inherited latent note (P3, not task-specific): agent calls retry up to _MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES=3 on schema-mismatched output, each with a fresh full timeout (judges.py:530-567), so the theoretical worst case exceeds the suite budget and an outer `timeout` kill discards all scored results (structural probe individual_outer_kill_loses_disk_checkpoint); this is identical under the template's batched 9000 and is not a task defect. Colderwater lessons checked for this row: 7 (repeat attempts add time; present), 9 (step reporting adds turns; present), 11 (judge infra timeouts zero criteria; individual mode limits that to one criterion, a plus), 19/20 (scripted golden is not judge duration; the index correctly labels it so). Lesson 10 (128 KB prompt) is not this row; the assembled per-session functional prompt is ~10 KB + 1.9 KB context + <=2.5 KB criterion.
counterexample: Conforming golden, plausible (not demonstrated): in the hro_unread_seen session the judge spends ~120-180 s on the mandatory backend check and context setup, then runs several negative legs that each watch 15 s and confirm in a fresh independent context, with one void timed attempt repeated; at ~8 s per GLM-flash tool round trip, ~70 calls exceed 600 s, asyncio.wait_for kills the session and the criterion scores 0.0 'judge timed out after 600s' although the app is correct (Oracle < 1). Weak app passing: none attributable to this row; timeouts can only under-credit.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, run the full configured verifier on the golden and record per-criterion functional session durations against 600 s; if any heavy criterion approaches the limit, reduce per-session workload (e.g. shorten the repeated in-dimension backend check or split/trim the heaviest criteria with matching public scope) or, with recorded lead authorization and a measured reason, adjust budgets below the five-hour cap while keeping judge sums < suite budgets < verifier timeout.
